discovery: Phase-sensitive Josephson-interference proof of d-wave pairing symmetry in high-temperature cuprate superconductors

nominees.name: Chang C. Tsuei
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

motivation: The symmetry of the Cooper pair wave function is the most basic property of a superconductor. For the cuprates it was hotly disputed until Van Harlingen's corner-SQUID and Josephson-junction interferometry, and then the tricrystal ring experiments of Tsuei and Kirtley, detected the sign change of the order parameter directly. The spontaneous half-integer flux quantum imaged in frustrated rings gave an unambiguous and model-independent proof of d(x2-y2) pairing. These experiments showed that the phase of the superconducting order parameter can be read out through Josephson physics. They set up the phase-sensitive approach now used to study Sr2RuO4, iron-based and heavy-fermion superconductors, pi-junctions, and topological and odd-frequency pairing at interfaces. The concept of a sign-changing unconventional order parameter now guides all searches for the pairing mechanism, and it also underlies superconducting pi-junction devices for quantum circuits.
